hub_a: ^Emex: You still think Luminar smiles because it cares.
^Emex: Give it time. The smile starts to feel like a mask.
a1: ^Emex: Luminar shines with knowledge and hope—so bright everyone in it is blind.
^Emex: If you don’t worship the mission, you’re treated like a defect.
^Emex: You become a problem they’re too polite to name.
a2: ^Emex: They’re not liars in the simple way.
^Emex: They believe their story so hard they stop seeing what doesn’t fit.
^Emex: And when you ask the wrong question, they smile and say, “I don’t know.”
^Emex: Because the answer would make you inconvenient.
a3: ^Emex: I’m tired of being told suffering is acceptable because the future will be perfect.
^Emex: I want people who can say, “this hurts,” without turning it into doctrine.
^Emex: Luminar talks about rebuilding the world.
hub_b: ^Emex: Hmmm… So you are one of them now.
^Emex: Don’t worry. That doesn’t mean you’re lost.
^Emex: It just means you stopped being impressed by speeches.
b_menu: ^What do you think the scholars are hiding?
^What should I watch out for in Luminar?
b1: ^Emex: But I’ve watched them dodge the same questions the same way—too polished.
^Emex: And I’ve watched Sanya turn uncertainty into confidence like it’s a magic trick.
^Emex: If you keep pushing, they’ll stop smiling.
^Emex: That’s when you’ll learn what “hope” looks like when it gets cornered.
b2: ^Emex: They’re rough, but they’re honest about what they are.
^Emex: Scholars talk like they’re saving everyone… even when nobody asked to be saved.
^Emex: Solace will tell you “no” to your face.
^Emex: Luminar will tell you “yes” and then decide what you’re allowed to hear.
b3: ^Emex: They don’t want you to be a person. They want you to be useful.
^Emex: Enjoy the kindness—just don’t confuse it with safety.
^Emex: And don’t let them make your questions feel childish.
